meta.title: The work — Nagy Habib
meta.description: Three lines of work of Professor Nagy Habib: hepatobiliary surgery, devices and life-science ventures, and translational research in liver disease.

sections.label: The work
sections.quote: Three sides of <t>one body of work.</t>
sections.sub: The surgery, the instruments and companies that came out of it, and the research that keeps feeding both.

sections.label: Engagements
sections.title: Where a conversation <t>usually begins.</t>
items: A liver, pancreatic or bile-duct case, and a referring clinician who wants the view of a surgeon who has operated on these organs for four decades.
A surgical device that works in the prototype, and a team that needs someone who has taken two from the theatre to the global market.
An RNA or gene-therapy programme for the liver that needs translational and clinical experience in the room.
A university spin-out facing licensing, regulation and its first partner, and a founder who has been through each.
A congress or symposium on hepatobiliary surgery, regenerative medicine or oligonucleotide therapeutics.
A journalist or a committee that needs the record in order, with dates and sources.

sections.label: Lines of work
sections.title: Three lines <t>of work.</t>
sections.lede: Each grounded in four decades at the same table.

cards.label: Surgery · Patients & referring clinicians
cards.title: What can be done for this liver?
cards.desc: Liver, pancreatic and bile-duct surgery at Hammersmith Hospital, by the surgeon whose radiofrequency technique made liver resection near-bloodless, and who performed the first living-related liver transplant in Africa and the Middle East.

cards.label: Devices & ventures · Founders, investors & industry
cards.title: How does an idea leave the theatre?
cards.desc: EMcision, a spin-out from Imperial, took two radiofrequency devices to market: the Habib 4X, with some 70,000 units sold, and the Habib EndoHPB, acquired with the company by Boston Scientific in 2018. Then companies in RNA activation, aptamers and gene therapy.

cards.label: Research & therapeutics · Universities, pharma & congresses
cards.title: What comes after the first trial?
cards.desc: Translational research in liver cancer and liver failure: adenovirus and plasmid gene therapy, autologous stem cells, and small activating RNA, from the first trials in patients to the companies that carry them forward.

sections.label: Through MiNA Therapeutics
sections.sub: Co-founded with Robert Habib, its founding Chief Executive since 2013. Small activating RNA raises the activity of a gene instead of silencing it; MTL-CEBPA, designed to restore C/EBP-α in the liver, was the first drug of its kind given to patients, in a phase I trial published in 2020. Professor Habib serves on the company’s Scientific Advisory Board.
